content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P0 - KV-cache surge + NCCL stalls on tp-gpu-pool. Elevated 5xx and latencies across host region us-west-2. Starting page at 2025-03-10T02:00Z.

sara (oncall): on it, acknowledging. paging ops (ben, jia). can someone pull recent srv logs + nvtop?

ben: grabbing logs from serving-rt-1..4. saw continuous-batching queue growth starting ~01:50Z, per-token cpu spike then GPU queuing.

jia: noticed a flurry of cache-miss storms for long-chat sessions; KV cache size jumped 6x in 10m for tp-shard groups. attaching snippet: `kv_cache_entries: 6_120_312 -> 37_254_001 in 10m`

mike: also seeing NCCL timeouts on tensor-parallel allreduce. error sample: `NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank returned unhandled cuda error` then `AllReduce timed out`. correlates with shard imbalance.

ben: hypothesis - continuous batching + aggressive prefix caching is causing many large KV entries, pushing uneven distribution across TP shards, causing NCCL to stall on straggler partitions.

opsbot: deploybot: recent change 2025-03-10T00:45Z rolled batching tweak BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=75 -> 5 and PREFETCH_ENABLED=true to enable aggressive kv prefetch.

jia: rolling back that batching tweak seems prudent. we can set PREFETCH_ENABLED=false and restore BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=75. planning config hotfix now.

sara (oncall): agreed. Ben/Jia, please coordinate hotfix. Mike, can you drop a temporary route to fallback model variant that doesn't use tp-sharded kv? we need to keep serving but reduce cross-GPU sync.

ben: preparing hotfix: patch config template in infra-configs -> serving/batching.yaml, change continuous_batching.enabled:false and set max_batch_tokens: 4096. applying to us-west-2 canary.

jia: canary applied to 2 nodes. metrics: cache entries down 30% in 3m, per-request p95 latency improved slightly but CPU still elevated.

mike: initiated fallback routing: requests for enterprise-1 and enterprise-3 pinned to non-tp-variant. CS notified.

customer-success: notifying affected customers with preliminary note: we see elevated latencies and intermittent 5xx from 01:50-02:15Z, mitigation in progress. will escalate if SLA breach likely.

eng-sre: observed NCCL stalls drop after disabling PREFETCH and increasing batch timeout. still see occasional AllReduce timeouts on a small set of shards (tp-shard-7, tp-shard-11). suspect shard mapping skew.

ben: digging into shard mapping tables. found that during the recent model version rollout, KV shard assignment script used a different hash seed leading to uneven partition sizes (tp-shard-7 holding 2.3x expected keys).

jia: that explains stragglers. fix options: 1) reassign keys and rebalance (heavy), 2) temporarily force replication for heavy partitions (fast), 3) degrade to single-GPU KV replica for affected traffic. prefer option 2+3 for immediate relief.

sara (oncall): go with replication for hot partitions + continue rollback of batching config. Ben/Jia implement replication rule `kv_replicate(shard_id)` for shards [7,11] and set `kv_shard_mode=replicated` for those.

ben: replication rule applied. metrics: packet losses down, NCCL timeouts gone for those shards. overall 5xx rate now within SLA thresholds.

opsbot: incident-bot: service health back to degraded->stable (partial) as of 02:20Z.

mike: rolling plan to restore normal serving: once traffic normalizes, we should re-run a balanced rehash with consistent seed and a controlled rebalance window. need to schedule offline rebalance to avoid another spike.

jane (eng-sre): (reacts :thumbsup:) this looks handled, pushing for postmortem.

customer-success: customers updated. one enterprise raised a support ticket - CS will own follow-up and timeline. no SLA breaches detected after mitigation.

sara (oncall): handing off to ben for next 8h follow-up. I'll update rotation and incident channel. ben, you take lead on root cause and postmortem doc.

ben: taking handoff. checklist:
- collect timeline + charts (kv entries, batch sizes, NCCL errors)
- diff deploy that changed hashing seed
- config changes (batching, prefetch) + ops runbooks used
- customer impact timeline for CS

jia: quick note: temp hotfixs: `PREFETCH_ENABLED=false`, `BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=75`, `continuous_batching.enabled=false`, `kv_shard_mode=replicated` for shards 7,11. rollback path documented in PR #9203.

mike: docker logs excerpt for debugging:```
[02:01:12Z] kv_sync: started rebalance attempt
[02:01:15Z] nccl: allreduce timeout (peer t7) -> watchdog kill
[02:02:03Z] batching: queue depth 9800 -> rate limit triggered
[02:03:44Z] cache: hotkey flood for conv_id=ch_9a3b... size=1.2M tokens
```

ben: adding this to incident timeline. planning postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 PDT. owners: ben (lead), jia (infra), mike (runtime), sara (ops review), cs lead for customer comms.

opsbot: Reminder: open follow-up ticket created INC-2025-347 in tracking.

sara (oncall): closing live incident channel. if anything reappears ping page again. great work everyone. :clap:

ben: will draft RCA, include mitigation steps and long-term fixes: consistent hashing enforcement, shard health autosignal (alert if partition >1.5x median), and safer batching defaults.

eng-sre: final note - recommend a test that simulates kv hotkey storms under tp-sharding to validate replication fallback and avoid NCCL stalls during future rollouts.

incident-bot: incident status: resolved (partial) at 2025-03-10T02:30Z. postmortem required.
